source.text: וּזְכֹר֙ אֶת־בּ֣וֹרְאֶ֔יךָ בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא־יָבֹ֨אוּ֙ יְמֵ֣י הָֽרָעָ֔ה וְהִגִּ֣יעוּ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר אֵֽין־לִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם חֵֽפֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And remember your Creator in [the] days of your youth, before that not come [the] days of the trouble and arrive years of which you will say, There is not to me in them pleasure,

en.L: And remember your Creator in the days of your youth, \q while the days of trouble have not [yet] come \q and the years [have not] arrived of which you will say, \q "I have no pleasure in them,"
en.B: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, \q while the days of trouble have not yet come \q and the years have not drawn near when you will say, \q "I find no pleasure in them,"
en.R: Remember the God who made you while you are still young, \q before the hard days come, \q before the years arrive when you will say, \q "I do not enjoy life anymore."

es.L: Y acuérdate de tu Creador en los días de tu juventud, \q mientras [aún] no lleguen los días de la desgracia \q y no se acerquen los años de los que dirás: \q «No tengo en ellos placer»,
es.B: Acuérdate de tu Creador en los días de tu juventud, \q mientras no hayan llegado los días difíciles \q ni se hayan acercado los años en que dirás: \q «No encuentro en ellos ningún gusto»,
es.R: Acuérdate del Dios que te hizo mientras todavía eres joven, \q antes de que lleguen los días duros, \q antes de que vengan los años en que dirás: \q «Ya no disfruto de la vida».

fr.L: Et souviens-toi de ton Créateur aux jours de ta jeunesse, \q tant que ne sont pas [encore] venus les jours du malheur \q et [que ne sont pas] arrivées les années dont tu diras : \q « Je n’ai en elles aucun plaisir »,
fr.B: Souviens-toi de ton Créateur aux jours de ta jeunesse, \q tant que les jours difficiles ne sont pas encore venus \q et que n’approchent pas les années où tu diras : \q « Je n’y trouve plus aucun plaisir »,
fr.R: Souviens-toi du Dieu qui t’a créé pendant que tu es encore jeune, \q avant que viennent les jours pénibles, \q avant qu’arrivent les années où tu diras : \q « Je n’ai plus de goût à la vie. »

sw.L: Nawe umkumbuke Muumba wako katika siku za ujana wako, \q maadamu siku za shida bado hazijafika \q na miaka bado haijawasili ambayo utaisema, \q "Sina raha nayo,"
sw.B: Mkumbuke Muumba wako ungali kijana, \q siku za shida zikiwa bado hazijaja, \q na miaka ikiwa bado haijakaribia ambayo utasema, \q "Haina raha kwangu,"
sw.R: Mkumbuke Mungu aliyekuumba ungali bado kijana, \q kabla siku ngumu hazijaja, \q kabla miaka haijafika ambapo utasema, \q "Sifurahii maisha tena."

vi.L: Và hãy nhớ Đấng Tạo Hóa của con trong những ngày tuổi trẻ của con, \q khi những ngày hoạn nạn chưa đến \q và những năm [chưa] tới mà về chúng con sẽ nói: \q "Tôi chẳng có vui thích gì trong chúng,"
vi.B: Hãy nhớ Đấng Tạo Hóa của con trong những ngày tuổi trẻ, \q khi những ngày khó khăn chưa đến \q và những năm tháng chưa tới gần, lúc con sẽ nói: \q "Tôi chẳng thấy vui thú gì trong những năm này,"
vi.R: Hãy nhớ đến Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng đã dựng nên con, khi con còn trẻ, \q trước khi những ngày khó nhọc đến, \q trước khi những năm tháng tới mà con sẽ nói: \q "Tôi chẳng còn thấy đời vui nữa."

ko.L: 또한 네 젊은 날들에 너의 창조주를 기억하여라. \q 재앙의 날들이 [아직] 오지 않고, \q "그 해들에는 내게 즐거움이 없다" 하고 \q 네가 말할 해들이 이르기 전에.
ko.B: 젊은 날에 너의 창조주를 기억하여라. \q 고난의 날들이 아직 오지 않았고, \q "사는 낙이 없다" 하고 \q 네가 말할 해들이 가까이 오기 전에.
ko.R: 아직 젊을 때 너를 지으신 하나님을 기억하여라. \q 힘든 날들이 오기 전에, \q "이제 사는 게 즐겁지 않다" 하고 \q 네가 말할 해들이 오기 전에 기억하여라.

pt.L: E lembre-se do seu Criador nos dias da sua mocidade, \q enquanto não chegarem os dias do mal \q e não se aproximarem os anos dos quais você dirá: \q "Não tenho prazer neles",
pt.B: Lembre-se do seu Criador enquanto você é jovem, \q enquanto os dias ruins ainda não chegaram \q e ainda não estão perto os anos em que você dirá: \q "Eles não me dão prazer nenhum",
pt.R: Lembre-se do Deus que fez você enquanto ainda é jovem, \q antes que cheguem os dias duros, \q antes que venham os anos em que você vai dizer: \q "Não tenho mais gosto pela vida."

am.L: ፈጣሪህንም በወጣትነትህ ቀኖች አስታውስ፤ \q የመከራ ቀኖች [ገና] ሳይመጡ፣ \q እንዲህ የምትልባቸውም ዓመታት ሳይደርሱ፦ \q «በእነርሱ ደስታ የለኝም፣»
am.B: በወጣትነትህ ዘመን ፈጣሪህን አስታውስ፤ \q የመከራ ቀኖች ገና ሳይመጡ፣ \q እንዲህ የምትልባቸው ዓመታትም ሳይቀርቡ፦ \q «በእነርሱ ደስ አልሰኝም፣»
am.R: ገና ወጣት ሳለህ የፈጠረህን እግዚአብሔርን አስታውስ፤ \q አስቸጋሪዎቹ ቀኖች ሳይመጡ፣ \q እንዲህ የምትልባቸው ዓመታት ሳይደርሱ፦ \q «ከእንግዲህ በሕይወት አልደሰትም።»

hi.L: और अपनी जवानी के दिनों में अपने रचनेवाले को स्मरण रखो, \q जब तक संकट के दिन [अभी] नहीं आए \q और वे वर्ष नहीं पहुँचे जिनके विषय में तुम कहोगे, \q "उनमें मुझे कोई सुख नहीं,"
hi.B: अपनी जवानी के दिनों में अपने सृष्टिकर्ता को याद रखो, \q जब तक कठिन दिन अभी आए नहीं \q और वे वर्ष निकट नहीं आए जब तुम कहोगे, \q "इनमें मुझे कोई आनंद नहीं मिलता,"
hi.R: जब तक तुम अभी जवान हो, उस परमेश्वर को याद रखो जिन्होंने तुम्हें बनाया, \q इससे पहले कि मुश्किल दिन आएँ, \q इससे पहले कि वे वर्ष आ पहुँचें जब तुम कहोगे, \q "अब जीने में मुझे कोई मज़ा नहीं आता।"

ru.L: И помни своего Творца во дни своей молодости, \q пока ещё не пришли дни беды \q и не настали годы, о которых ты скажешь: \q «Нет мне в них отрады»,
ru.B: Помни своего Творца в дни юности, \q пока не пришли дни беды \q и не приблизились годы, когда ты скажешь: \q «Мне в них нет радости»,
ru.R: Помни Бога, который сотворил тебя, пока ты ещё молод, \q пока не пришли тяжёлые дни, \q пока не настали годы, когда ты скажешь: \q «Жизнь мне больше не в радость.»

uk.L: І памʼятай твого Творця в дні твоєї молодості, \q поки не прийшли дні лиха \q і [не] настали роки, про які скажеш: \q «Немає мені в них утіхи»,
uk.B: Памʼятай свого Творця в дні своєї молодості, \q поки ще не прийшли дні лиха \q і не наблизилися роки, коли ти скажеш: \q «Немає мені в них утіхи»,
uk.R: Памʼятай Бога, який тебе створив, поки ти ще молодий, \q поки не прийшли тяжкі дні, \q поки не настали роки, коли ти скажеш: \q «Я вже не тішуся життям.»

decisions.choice: your Creator: God, who made you
alternatives: your well (your wife, as in Proverbs 5:15-18)
decisions.reason: The word is the participle of the verb used in Genesis 1:1 for God's creating. Its form is plural, which may be a plural of majesty, as "God" itself is plural in form. Because the letters are close to the words for "well" and "pit", some have read "remember your well" (your wife, as in Proverbs 5:15) or "remember your grave". The usual reading, "your Creator", fits the call to live before God (11:9; 12:7).

decisions.choice: the days of trouble: the hard days of old age
decisions.reason: The word (*ra'ah*) here is trouble or misfortune, not moral evil. The verses that follow picture those days.

decisions.choice: before: the start of one long sentence that runs to verse 7
decisions.reason: "Before" begins a series of pictures of old age and death, and comes back in verses 2 and 6. All of verses 1-7 hang on the command "remember your Creator". This poem closes Qoheleth's own words.

decisions.choice: I have no pleasure in them: there is no joy left in life
decisions.reason: The years of old age, when the strength to enjoy life is gone (2 Samuel 19:36).

decisions.choice: the God who made you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the Creator is.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on to verse 7, so Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma. Readable makes shorter sentences.

decisions.choice: each verse of the poem (12:1-7) closed as a sentence of its own
alternatives: one sentence running from verse 1 to verse 7
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is one long sentence hanging on "remember". Korean ends a sentence with its verb, so a sentence across seven verses would put the command at the very end; each verse is closed instead, with the command or "그리하여라" repeated where needed, as these books do where a Hebrew sentence runs across verses.

decisions.choice: lembre-se ... enquanto não chegarem (L); enquanto você é jovem ... enquanto ... ainda não (B)
alternatives: antes que venham os maus dias
decisions.reason: The poem of 12:1-7 is among the best-known passages of the book, and its familiar Portuguese wording pulls hard. Each level is drafted from the Hebrew and the English reading: Literal keeps "mocidade" and "os dias do mal" (m2), Balanced turns "before" into "enquanto ... ainda não", which says the same thing from the side of the young reader.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The English capitalises pronouns for God as a reader setting. The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change in Amharic and the text has no span. This holds through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "ፈጣሪህን ... አስታውስ" (remember your Creator)
decisions.reason: The poem of 12:1-7 is drafted fresh from the Hebrew. "አስታውስ" says "remember" plainly; Readable says "የፈጠረህን እግዚአብሔርን" (the God who made you), as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: the "before" clauses as "ሳይ-" verbs ending each line (12:1-2, 6)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "before" governs one long sentence to verse 7. Amharic says it with the negative converb ("ሳይመጡ", "ሳይጨልሙ", "ሳይበጠስ"), which can close each line and so keeps the lines apart; the quotation in verse 1 follows "እንዲህ የምትልባቸው" so that it ends the verse, as in the English. Readable closes verses 2 and 6 with "አስታውሰው" (remember him), as its English does.

decisions.choice: the poem of 12:1-7 is drafted from the Hebrew: "अपने रचनेवाले" (L), "अपने सृष्टिकर्ता" (B), "उस परमेश्वर ... जिन्होंने तुम्हें बनाया" (R)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-7 are one long sentence about old age and death (m3), which each level drafts from the Hebrew and its gloss so that it does not follow the wording of older Hindi Bibles. Literal and Balanced keep the sentence running to verse 7 with commas, as the English does; Readable makes shorter sentences and repeats "remember him" (verses 2 and 6). The Creator is God, who made you (m1); Readable says so plainly, with the honorific "जिन्होंने". The young reader is addressed with "तुम", as in 11:9.

decisions.choice: the poem of 12:1-7 drafted from the gloss
decisions.reason: The poem on old age pulls hard toward the familiar Synodal wording; it is drafted from the Hebrew and the meaning decisions, with its own words for the images. Literal and Balanced keep it one long sentence to verse 7, ending each verse with a comma; Readable makes shorter sentences (m3).

decisions.choice: Бога, который сотворил тебя
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the Creator is (m1).

decisions.choice: "Творець" (L, B), "Бог, який тебе створив" (R); the images of 12:1-7 kept as they stand at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: "Творець" is the Ukrainian word for God as maker. The poem on old age is one long sentence; each level keeps the English sentence shape and line breaks, and the images (the house, the grinders, the silver cord) keep their words, with their meaning left to the meaning decisions.

source.text: עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־תֶחְשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ וְהָא֔וֹר וְהַיָּרֵ֖חַ וְהַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים וְשָׁ֥בוּ הֶעָבִ֖ים אַחַ֥ר הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: before that not is darkened the sun and the light and the moon and the stars, and return the clouds after the rain,

en.L: before the sun is darkened, and the light, \q and the moon and the stars, \q and the clouds return after the rain,
en.B: before the sun grows dark, and the light, \q and the moon and the stars, \q and the clouds return after the rain,
en.R: Remember him before the sun and its light \q and the moon and the stars grow dark, \q and the clouds come back after the rain.

es.L: antes de que se ensombrezca el sol, y la luz, \q y la luna y las estrellas, \q y regresen las nubes después de la lluvia,
es.B: antes de que el sol pierda su brillo, y también la luz, \q la luna y las estrellas, \q y las nubes regresen tras la lluvia,
es.R: Acuérdate de Dios antes de que el sol y su luz \q y la luna y las estrellas se oscurezcan, \q y las nubes vuelvan después de la lluvia.

fr.L: avant que ne s’assombrisse le soleil, et la lumière, \q et la lune et les étoiles, \q et que les nuages ne reviennent à la suite de la pluie,
fr.B: avant que le soleil ne perde son éclat, et la lumière, \q et la lune et les étoiles, \q et que les nuages ne reviennent sitôt la pluie passée,
fr.R: Souviens-toi de Dieu avant que le soleil et sa lumière, \q la lune et les étoiles ne s’éteignent, \q et que les nuages ne reviennent après la pluie.

sw.L: maadamu jua halijafanywa giza, wala nuru, \q wala mwezi na nyota, \q wala mawingu hayajarejea nyuma ya mvua,
sw.B: kabla jua halijafifia, pamoja na nuru, \q na mwezi na nyota, \q na mawingu kurejea baada ya mvua,
sw.R: Mkumbuke Mungu kabla jua na mwanga wake, \q mwezi na nyota havijafifia, \q na mawingu kurudi baada ya mvua.

vi.L: trước khi mặt trời bị tối tăm, và ánh sáng, \q và mặt trăng và các ngôi sao, \q và mây kéo trở lại sau cơn mưa,
vi.B: trước khi mặt trời tối sầm, cả ánh sáng nữa, \q cả mặt trăng và các vì sao, \q và mây lại kéo về sau cơn mưa,
vi.R: Hãy nhớ đến Đức Chúa Trời trước khi mặt trời và ánh sáng của nó, \q mặt trăng và các vì sao trở nên tối tăm, \q và mây lại kéo về sau cơn mưa.

ko.L: 해와 빛과 \q 달과 별들이 어두워지고, \q 비 온 뒤에 구름이 다시 돌아오기 전에 [그리하여라].
ko.B: 해와 빛이, \q 달과 별들이 어두워지기 전에, \q 비가 그친 뒤에 다시 구름이 몰려오기 전에 그리하여라.
ko.R: 해와 햇빛과 \q 달과 별들이 어두워지기 전에, \q 비가 온 뒤에 다시 구름이 몰려오기 전에 하나님을 기억하여라.

pt.L: antes que o sol escureça, e a luz, \q e a lua e as estrelas, \q e as nuvens retornem depois da chuva,
pt.B: antes que se apaguem o sol e a luz, \q a lua e as estrelas, \q e as nuvens tornem depois da chuva,
pt.R: Lembre-se dele antes que o sol e a sua luz \q e a lua e as estrelas fiquem escuros, \q e as nuvens voltem depois da chuva.

am.L: ፀሐይና ብርሃን፣ \q ጨረቃና ከዋክብትም ሳይጨልሙ፣ \q ደመናዎችም ከዝናብ በኋላ ሳይመለሱ፣
am.B: ፀሐይና ብርሃን፣ \q ጨረቃና ከዋክብትም ሳይጨልሙ፣ \q ደመናዎችም ከዝናብ በኋላ ተመልሰው ሳይመጡ፣
am.R: ፀሐይና ብርሃኗ፣ \q ጨረቃና ከዋክብትም ሳይጨልሙ፣ \q ደመናዎችም ከዝናብ በኋላ ተመልሰው ሳይመጡ አስታውሰው።

hi.L: इससे पहले कि सूर्य अंधियारा हो जाए, और उजियाला, \q और चंद्रमा और तारे, \q और वर्षा के बाद बादल फिर लौट आएँ,
hi.B: इससे पहले कि सूर्य धुँधला पड़ जाए, और उजियाला भी, \q और चंद्रमा और तारे भी, \q और वर्षा के बाद फिर बादल घिर आएँ,
hi.R: उन्हें याद रखो, इससे पहले कि सूर्य और उसका उजाला \q और चाँद और तारे अंधेरे पड़ जाएँ, \q और बारिश के बाद फिर से बादल छा जाएँ।

ru.L: прежде чем затмится солнце, и свет, \q и луна, и звёзды, \q и тучи возвратятся после дождя,
ru.B: прежде чем потемнеет солнце и свет, \q и луна, и звёзды, \q и тучи вернутся после дождя,
ru.R: Помни {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, пока солнце и его свет, \q луна и звёзды не потемнели, \q а тучи не стали возвращаться после дождя.

uk.L: поки не потемніло сонце, і світло, \q і місяць, і зорі, \q і не повернулися хмари після дощу,

decisions.choice: the lights grow dark: the darkening of life as old age and death come near
alternatives: the darkness of the end of the world
decisions.reason: The sun, moon and stars going dark is the language the prophets use for the day of judgment (Isaiah 13:10; Joel 2:10). Here it pictures the end of one life: light and joy fade (11:7-8). Some read it more narrowly as failing eyesight, or as the dark days of winter.

decisions.choice: the clouds return after the rain: storm after storm, with no clearing
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel the rains come in winter. Clouds that return after the rain are the dreary days of winter, when one storm follows another. Old age is pictured as a winter with no spring after it.

records.literal_gloss: in the day that tremble [the] keepers of the house, and bend [the] men of the strength, and cease the grinders because they are few, and are darkened those looking through the windows,

en.L: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, \q and the men of strength bend, \q and the grinding women stop because they are few, \q and those [women] who look through the windows grow dark,
en.B: on the day when the guards of the house tremble \q and the strong men stoop, \q when the women who grind stop because they are few, \q and the women who look through the windows see only dimly,
en.R: That is when the guards of the house will tremble \q and the strong men will be bent over. \q The women who grind the grain will stop, because there are only a few of them, \q and the women who look out the windows will hardly see.

es.L: en el día en que tiemblen los guardianes de la casa, \q y se doblen los hombres de fuerza, \q y cesen las que muelen porque son pocas, \q y se oscurezcan las [mujeres] que miran por las ventanas,
es.B: el día en que tiemblen los guardias de la casa \q y se doblen los hombres fuertes, \q cuando las mujeres que muelen se detengan por ser pocas, \q y las que miran por las ventanas apenas vean,
es.R: Entonces temblarán los guardias de la casa \q y los hombres fuertes andarán encorvados. \q Las mujeres que muelen el grano dejarán de hacerlo, porque quedan pocas, \q y las mujeres que miran por las ventanas casi no verán.

fr.L: au jour où tremblent les gardiens de la maison, \q et où se courbent les hommes de force, \q et où cessent les meunières parce qu’elles sont peu nombreuses, \q et où s’obscurcissent celles qui regardent par les fenêtres,
fr.B: le jour où les gardes de la maison tremblent \q et où les hommes forts se voûtent, \q où les femmes qui moulent le grain s’arrêtent parce qu’elles sont trop peu, \q et où les femmes qui regardent par les fenêtres ne voient plus que confusément,
fr.R: C’est alors que les gardes de la maison trembleront \q et que les hommes forts seront courbés. \q Les femmes qui moulent le grain s’arrêteront, parce qu’il n’en reste que quelques-unes, \q et les femmes qui regardent par les fenêtres ne verront presque plus rien.

ko.L: 그날에 집의 파수꾼들이 떨고, \q 힘의 사내들이 구부러지며, \q 맷돌 가는 여인들은 적어서 멈추고, \q 창들로 내다보는 [여인들]은 어두워진다.

am.L: የቤቱ ጠባቂዎች በሚንቀጠቀጡበት፣ \q ብርቱዎቹም ሰዎች በሚጎብጡበት፣ \q ፈጪዎቹ ሴቶችም ጥቂቶች ስለ ሆኑ በሚያቆሙበት፣ \q በመስኮቶችም የሚመለከቱት [ሴቶች] በሚጨልሙበት ቀን፣
am.B: የቤቱ ዘበኞች በሚንቀጠቀጡበትና \q ብርቱዎቹ ሰዎች በሚጎብጡበት ቀን፣ \q የሚፈጩት ሴቶች ጥቂቶች ስለ ሆኑ በሚያቆሙበትና \q በመስኮት የሚመለከቱት ሴቶች አጥርተው ማየት በማይችሉበት ጊዜ፣
am.R: ያን ጊዜ የቤቱ ዘበኞች ይንቀጠቀጣሉ፤ \q ብርቱዎቹም ሰዎች ይጎብጣሉ። \q እህል የሚፈጩት ሴቶች ጥቂቶች ብቻ ስለ ቀሩ ሥራቸውን ያቆማሉ፤ \q በመስኮት የሚመለከቱትም ሴቶች በጭንቅ ያያሉ።

ru.L: в день, когда затрепещут сторожа дома, \q и сгорбятся сильные мужчины, \q и оставят работу мелющие [женщины], потому что их мало, \q и потемнеют глядящие [женщины] сквозь окна,
ru.B: в день, когда задрожат охранники дома \q и сгорбятся сильные мужчины, \q когда перестанут молоть женщины, потому что их мало, \q и женщины, глядящие из окон, будут видеть лишь смутно,

uk.L: у день, коли тремтітимуть сторожі дому, \q і зігнуться мужі сили, \q і перестануть мелючі, бо їх мало, \q і потемніють ті, що дивляться крізь вікна,
uk.B: у день, коли тремтітимуть сторожі дому \q і згорбляться сильні чоловіки, \q коли жінки, що мелють, перестануть, бо їх мало, \q і ті, що дивляться у вікна, бачитимуть тьмяно,
uk.R: Тоді тремтітимуть сторожі дому \q і згорбляться сильні чоловіки. \q Жінки, що мелють зерно, перестануть, бо їх лишилося мало, \q а ті, що виглядають у вікна, ледве бачитимуть.

decisions.choice: the house: a great house falling into decay and silence, a picture of old age and death
alternatives: the body of an old person: arms, legs, teeth and eyes
a household in mourning after a death
a city or community in decline
decisions.reason: Verses 3-5 picture a large house where everything is failing: the guards tremble, the strong men stoop, the women who grind grain stop, the women at the windows can no longer see, the doors are shut and the sound of the mill dies away. Readers have long differed on what the picture means. An old reading, both Jewish and Christian, takes each part as a part of the aging body: the keepers are the arms and hands, the strong men the legs, the grinders the teeth, those at the windows the eyes, the doors the ears or lips. Others read it as a real household struck by death, or as a picture of decline in general. The translation keeps the pictures as the poem gives them.

decisions.choice: the grinders: the women who grind grain at the hand mill
decisions.reason: The word is feminine. Grinding grain each morning at a hand mill was women's work (Exodus 11:5). On the reading of the house as the body, the grinders are the teeth, few and no longer able to chew. This is one of the images on which readers differ (m1).

decisions.choice: those who look through the windows grow dark: the women at the windows can no longer see
decisions.reason: The participle is feminine: women looking out of the lattice windows (Judges 5:28). Their growing dark is often read as the eyes losing their sight.

decisions.choice: the keepers of the house and the men of strength: the guards and the strong men of the household
decisions.reason: The keepers protect the house; the strong men carry its burdens. They tremble and stoop. On the reading of the house as the body, they are the hands and arms, and the legs.

decisions.choice: the grinding women ... those [women] who look (L); the women who grind ... the women who look (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are feminine (m2, m3), so the renderings say "women". They keep the pictures and do not choose between the readings in m1.

decisions.choice: "पीसनेवालियाँ ... झाँकनेवालियाँ" (L); "पीसनेवाली स्त्रियाँ ... झाँकनेवाली स्त्रियाँ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are feminine (m2, m3), and Hindi shows it in the forms. As in the English, every level keeps the pictures of the decaying house and does not explain them as parts of the body, since the reading is not certain (m1).

decisions.choice: [женщины] (L); женщины (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words for the grinders and those at the windows are feminine (m2, m3), which Russian participles in the plural do not show; Literal brackets женщины, Balanced and Readable say it. The renderings keep the pictures of the house and do not choose between readings of what they stand for (m1).

source.text: וְסֻגְּר֤וּ דְלָתַ֨יִם֙ בַּשּׁ֔וּק בִּשְׁפַ֖ל ק֣וֹל הַֽטַּחֲנָ֑ה וְיָקוּם֙ לְק֣וֹל הַצִּפּ֔וֹר וְיִשַּׁ֖חוּ כָּל־בְּנ֥וֹת הַשִּֽׁיר׃

records.literal_gloss: and are shut [the] doors in the street, when [is] low [the] sound of the grinding, and one rises at [the] sound of the bird, and are brought low all [the] daughters of the song,

en.L: and the doors on the street are shut, \q when the sound of the grinding is low, \q and one rises at the sound of the bird, \q and all the daughters of song are brought low,
en.B: when the doors on the street are closed \q and the noise of grinding fades, \q when people rise at the sound of a bird, \q and all the songs grow faint,
en.R: The doors to the street will be closed, \q and the sound of the mill will grow quiet. \q People will wake up when a bird sings, \q and all the songs will fade away.

es.L: y se cierren las puertas a la calle, \q cuando baje el sonido del molino, \q y uno se levante a la voz del ave, \q y se abatan todas las hijas del canto,
es.B: cuando se cierren las puertas que dan a la calle \q y se apague el ruido del molino, \q cuando la gente se levante al canto de un pájaro \q y todos los cantos se debiliten,
es.R: Las puertas que dan a la calle se cerrarán, \q y el ruido del molino se irá callando. \q La gente se despertará cuando cante un pájaro, \q y todas las canciones se irán apagando.

fr.L: et où les portes sur la rue sont fermées, \q quand le bruit de la meule baisse, \q et qu’on se lève à la voix de l’oiseau, \q et que toutes les filles du chant s’affaiblissent,
fr.B: quand les portes sur la rue se ferment \q et que le bruit de la meule s’éteint, \q quand on se lève au chant d’un oiseau \q et que tous les chants s’affaiblissent,
fr.R: Les portes qui donnent sur la rue seront fermées, \q et le bruit du moulin se fera plus faible. \q Les gens se réveilleront dès qu’un oiseau chantera, \q et tous les chants s’éteindront peu à peu.

sw.L: na milango ya kuelekea njiani inafungwa, \q sauti ya kusaga inapokuwa chini, \q na mtu anaamka kwa sauti ya ndege, \q na binti wote wa wimbo wanashushwa,
sw.B: milango ya kuelekea barabarani inapofungwa \q na sauti ya kusaga inapofifia, \q watu wanapoamka kwa sauti ya ndege \q na nyimbo zote zinaposikika hafifu,
sw.R: Milango inayoelekea barabarani itafungwa, \q na sauti ya kinu itapungua. \q Watu wataamka ndege anapolia, \q na nyimbo zote zitafifia.

vi.L: và các cửa ngoài đường bị đóng lại, \q khi tiếng cối xay nhỏ dần, \q và người ta thức dậy theo tiếng chim, \q và mọi con gái của bài ca bị hạ thấp,
vi.B: khi các cửa ngoài đường đóng lại \q và tiếng cối xay lịm dần, \q khi người ta thức dậy vì tiếng chim kêu \q và mọi tiếng hát đều yếu ớt,
vi.R: Các cửa ra đường sẽ đóng lại, \q và tiếng cối xay sẽ lặng dần. \q Người ta sẽ thức giấc khi chim hót, \q và mọi tiếng hát sẽ tắt dần.

ko.L: 거리로 난 문들이 닫히고, \q 맷돌 소리가 낮아지며, \q 새 소리에 [사람이] 일어나고, \q 노래의 딸들이 모두 낮아진다.
ko.B: 거리로 난 문들이 닫히고 \q 맷돌 소리가 잦아들며, \q 사람들이 새 소리에 잠을 깨고 \q 모든 노랫소리가 희미해진다.
ko.R: 거리로 난 문들이 닫히고 \q 맷돌 소리가 작아진다. \q 사람들은 새가 지저귀면 잠에서 깨고, \q 모든 노랫소리가 사라져 간다.

pt.L: e as portas para a rua se fecharem, \q quando o som da moagem baixar, \q e alguém se levantar ao som do pássaro, \q e todas as filhas do canto se abaterem,
pt.B: quando as portas da rua se fecharem \q e o barulho do moinho enfraquecer, \q quando as pessoas se levantarem com o canto de um pássaro \q e todas as canções sumirem,
pt.R: As portas da rua vão ficar fechadas, \q e o barulho do moinho vai diminuir. \q As pessoas vão acordar quando um pássaro cantar, \q e todas as canções vão sumir.

am.L: በጎዳናም ያሉ በሮች ሲዘጉ፣ \q የወፍጮውም ድምፅ ሲቀንስ፣ \q በወፍ ድምፅ ሲነሣ፣ \q የዘፈን ሴቶች ልጆችም ሁሉ ዝቅ ሲሉ፣
am.B: በጎዳና ላይ ያሉ በሮች ሲዘጉ፣ \q የወፍጮው ድምፅ ሲደክም፣ \q ሰዎች በወፍ ድምፅ ሲነሡ፣ \q ዘፈኖችም ሁሉ ሲደበዝዙ፣
am.R: ወደ ጎዳና የሚያወጡት በሮች ይዘጋሉ፤ \q የወፍጮውም ድምፅ ጸጥ ይላል። \q ሰዎች ወፍ ሲዘምር ይነቃሉ፤ \q ዘፈኖችም ሁሉ እየደከሙ ይጠፋሉ።

hi.L: और गली की ओर के द्वार बंद हो जाएँ, \q जब चक्की की आवाज़ धीमी हो, \q और कोई पक्षी की आवाज़ पर उठ बैठे, \q और गीत की सब बेटियाँ नीची पड़ जाएँ,
hi.B: जब गली के द्वार बंद कर दिए जाएँ \q और चक्की का शोर मंद पड़ जाए, \q जब लोग किसी पक्षी के बोलते ही जाग उठें, \q और सब गीत धीमे पड़ जाएँ,
hi.R: गली की ओर खुलनेवाले दरवाज़े बंद हो जाएँगे, \q और चक्की की आवाज़ धीमी पड़ जाएगी। \q किसी पक्षी के गाते ही लोग जाग जाएँगे, \q और सब गीत मंद होकर खो जाएँगे।

ru.L: и будут заперты двери на улицу, \q когда ослабнет шум помола, \q и поднимутся на голос птицы, \q и поникнут все дочери песни,
ru.B: когда закроются двери на улицу \q и затихнет шум жерновов, \q когда люди будут вставать от птичьего голоса \q и все песни станут едва слышны,
ru.R: Двери на улицу закроются, \q и шум мельницы затихнет. \q Люди будут просыпаться, когда запоёт птица, \q и все песни смолкнут.

uk.L: і зачиняться двері на вулицю, \q коли стихне звук жорен, \q і встають на голос птаха, \q і принишкнуть усі дочки пісні,
uk.B: коли зачинять двері на вулицю \q і стихне шум жорен, \q коли люди встають від голосу птаха \q і стихають усі пісні,
uk.R: Двері на вулицю будуть зачинені, \q і звук млина стихне. \q Люди прокидатимуться, коли заспіває птах, \q і всі пісні стихнуть.

decisions.choice: the doors shut and the sound of grinding low: the house falls silent
alternatives: the ears grow deaf, or the lips close over toothless gums
decisions.reason: The doors of the house onto the street are closed, and the daily sound of the mill dies away. On the reading of the house as the body (verse 3), the doors are the ears or the lips, and the faint grinding is the chewing of an old mouth. See the main note on the images of the poem at verse 3.

decisions.choice: one rises at the sound of the bird: the old wake at the first birdsong
alternatives: the voice rises to the thin pitch of a bird
the bird's voice rises (in a funeral lament)
decisions.reason: The verb has no clear subject. It is most often read as the old person waking at the first bird of dawn, unable to sleep. Others read that the voice of the old becomes thin like a bird's, or that the sound of a bird rises over the silent house.

decisions.choice: the daughters of song: songs, or singing women
decisions.reason: "Daughters of" can name the members of a group, so "daughters of song" may be the notes of songs or the women who sing them. They are "brought low": they grow faint, perhaps because the old can no longer hear them (2 Samuel 19:36).

decisions.choice: all the songs grow faint (B); all the songs will fade away (R)
alternatives: all the daughters of song are brought low
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m3). Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: people rise (B); people will wake up (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no stated subject (m2). Balanced and Readable say "people", which keeps the most common reading without naming a body part.

decisions.choice: "सब गीत"
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means, songs (m3); Literal keeps "गीत की बेटियाँ". Balanced and Readable say "लोग" for the unstated subject (m2).

decisions.choice: все песни станут едва слышны (B); все песни смолкнут (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means, songs or singing women (m3); Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: люди
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no stated subject (m2); Balanced and Readable say люди.

records.literal_gloss: also of height they are afraid, and terrors [are] in the way, and blossoms the almond, and drags itself along the grasshopper, and fails the caper-berry; for goes the human to [the] house of his eternity, and go around in the street the mourners,

en.L: also of a height they are afraid, and terrors [are] on the way, \q and the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, \q and the caper-berry fails; \q for {{gender:the human|man}} goes to {{gender:their|his}} eternal house, \q and the mourners go around in the street,
en.B: when people are afraid of heights and of dangers on the road, \q when the almond tree blossoms and the grasshopper drags itself along, \q and the caper-berry no longer stirs desire, \q because everyone goes to their eternal home, \q and mourners go about in the streets,
en.R: People will be afraid of high places and of dangers in the street. \q The almond tree will blossom, and the grasshopper will drag itself along, \q and desire will be gone. \q All this happens because people are going to their everlasting home, \q and mourners walk around in the streets.

es.L: también de la altura tienen miedo, y terrores [hay] en el camino, \q y florece el almendro, y se arrastra el saltamontes, \q y falla la alcaparra; \q porque {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} va a su casa eterna, \q y los que hacen duelo rondan por la calle,
es.B: cuando se teme a las alturas y a los peligros del camino, \q cuando florece el almendro y el saltamontes se arrastra, \q y la alcaparra ya no despierta el deseo, \q porque todos van a su morada eterna, \q y los que lloran a los muertos recorren las calles,
es.R: La gente tendrá miedo de los lugares altos y de los peligros de la calle. \q El almendro florecerá, y el saltamontes se arrastrará, \q y el deseo desaparecerá. \q Todo esto pasa porque la gente va camino a su hogar eterno, \q y los que lloran a los muertos andan por las calles.

fr.L: on a peur aussi de la hauteur, et des terreurs [sont] sur le chemin, \q et l’amandier fleurit, et la sauterelle se traîne, \q et le câprier défaille ; \q car {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} se rend à sa maison d’éternité, \q et les gens en deuil tournent dans la rue,
fr.B: quand on craint les hauteurs et les dangers de la route, \q quand l’amandier est en fleur et que la sauterelle se traîne, \q et que la câpre n’éveille plus le désir, \q parce que chacun s’en va vers sa demeure de toujours, \q et que les gens en deuil vont et viennent dans les rues,
fr.R: On aura peur des endroits élevés et des dangers de la rue. \q L’amandier fleurira, et la sauterelle se traînera, \q et le désir aura disparu. \q Tout cela arrive parce que les gens s’en vont vers leur demeure pour toujours, \q et que ceux qui pleurent les morts passent dans les rues.

sw.L: pia wanaogopa kimo, na hofu [ziko] njiani, \q na mlozi unachanua, na panzi anajikokota, \q na tunda la kaperi linakoma; \q kwa maana mwanadamu anakwenda kwenye nyumba yake ya milele, \q na waombolezaji wanazunguka barabarani,
sw.B: watu wanapoogopa mahali palipoinuka na hatari za njiani, \q mlozi unapochanua na panzi anapojikokota, \q na tunda la kaperi halichochei tena tamaa, \q kwa sababu kila mtu anakwenda kwenye makao yake ya milele, \q na waombolezaji wanazunguka barabarani,
sw.R: Watu wataogopa mahali palipo juu na hatari za barabarani. \q Mlozi utachanua maua, na panzi atajikokota, \q na hamu itatoweka. \q Haya yote yanatokea kwa sababu watu wanakwenda kwenye makao yao ya milele, \q na waombolezaji wanatembea barabarani.

vi.L: cũng sợ chỗ cao, và những nỗi kinh hãi [ở] trên đường, \q và cây hạnh nở hoa, và cào cào lê mình, \q và trái bạch hoa mất hiệu lực; \q vì con người đi đến nhà đời đời của mình, \q và những người khóc tang đi quanh ngoài đường,
vi.B: khi người ta sợ chỗ cao và những hiểm nguy dọc đường, \q khi cây hạnh nở hoa và cào cào lê bước nặng nề, \q và trái bạch hoa chẳng còn khơi dậy ham muốn, \q vì ai nấy đều đi về ngôi nhà vĩnh cửu của mình, \q và những người khóc tang đi lại ngoài phố,
vi.R: Người ta sẽ sợ chỗ cao và sợ những hiểm nguy ngoài đường. \q Cây hạnh sẽ nở hoa, cào cào sẽ lê mình, \q và mọi ham muốn sẽ không còn. \q Mọi điều ấy xảy ra vì người ta đang đi về ngôi nhà đời đời của mình, \q và những người khóc tang đi lại ngoài phố.

ko.L: 또한 높은 곳을 두려워하고, 길에는 두려움이 [있으며], \q 아몬드나무가 꽃을 피우고, 메뚜기가 몸을 끌며, \q 케이퍼 열매가 효력을 잃는다. \q 사람이 제 영원한 처소로 가고, \q 곡하는 이들이 거리를 오가기 때문이다.
ko.B: 사람들은 높은 곳을 두려워하고 길에서 만날 위험을 무서워하며, \q 아몬드나무에 꽃이 피고 메뚜기는 힘겹게 기어가며, \q 케이퍼 열매도 더는 입맛을 돋우지 못한다. \q 누구나 영원히 머물 집으로 가고, \q 곡하는 이들이 거리를 오가기 때문이다.
ko.R: 사람들은 높은 곳을 무서워하고 거리의 위험을 두려워한다. \q 아몬드나무에 꽃이 피고, 메뚜기는 힘겹게 기어간다. \q 그리고 바라는 마음도 사라진다. \q 이 모든 것은 사람이 영원히 머물 집으로 가고 있기 때문이다. \q 그래서 곡하는 사람들이 거리를 오간다.

pt.L: também da altura terão medo, e [haverá] terrores no caminho, \q e a amendoeira florescerá, e o gafanhoto se arrastará, \q e a alcaparra falhará; \q pois {{gender:o ser humano|o homem}} vai para a sua casa eterna, \q e os que fazem luto circulam pela rua,
pt.B: quando as pessoas tiverem medo de lugares altos e dos perigos do caminho, \q quando a amendoeira florir e o gafanhoto se arrastar, \q e a alcaparra já não despertar o desejo, \q porque todos vão para a sua morada eterna, \q e os que choram os mortos andam pelas ruas,
pt.R: As pessoas vão ter medo de lugares altos e dos perigos da rua. \q A amendoeira vai florir, e o gafanhoto vai se arrastar, \q e o desejo vai acabar. \q Tudo isso acontece porque as pessoas estão indo para o seu lar eterno, \q e os que choram os mortos andam pelas ruas.

am.L: ደግሞም ከፍታን ይፈራሉ፤ በመንገድም ላይ ድንጋጤዎች [አሉ]፤ \q የለውዝ ዛፍም ያብባል፤ አንበጣውም ራሱን እየጎተተ ይሄዳል፤ \q የካፐር ፍሬውም ይከስማል፤ \q ሰው ወደ ዘላለም ቤቱ ይሄዳልና፤ \q አልቃሾችም በጎዳና ይዞራሉ፤
am.B: ሰዎች ከፍታን፣ በመንገድም ያሉ አደጋዎችን ሲፈሩ፣ \q የለውዝ ዛፍ ሲያብብና አንበጣው ራሱን እየጎተተ ሲሄድ፣ \q ፍላጎትን የሚቀሰቅሰው ፍሬ ከእንግዲህ ሳይሠራ ሲቀር፣ \q ሁሉም ወደ ዘላለም ቤቱ ይሄዳልና፤ \q አልቃሾችም በጎዳናዎች ይዞራሉ፤
am.R: ሰዎች ከፍ ያሉ ስፍራዎችንና በመንገድ ያሉ አደጋዎችን ይፈራሉ። \q የለውዝ ዛፍ ያብባል፤ አንበጣውም ራሱን እየጎተተ ይሄዳል፤ \q ፍላጎትም ይጠፋል። \q ይህ ሁሉ የሚሆነው ሰዎች ወደ ዘላለም ቤታቸው ስለሚሄዱ ነው፤ \q አልቃሾችም በጎዳናዎች ይዞራሉ።

hi.L: वे ऊँचाई से भी डरें, और मार्ग में भय [हों], \q और बादाम का पेड़ फूले, और टिड्डा घिसटता चले, \q और कबरबेरी बेअसर हो जाए; \q क्योंकि मनुष्य अपने सनातन घर को जाता है, \q और विलाप करनेवाले गली में घूमते हैं,
hi.B: जब लोग ऊँचाइयों से और मार्ग के ख़तरों से डरें, \q जब बादाम का पेड़ फूले और टिड्डा घिसट-घिसटकर चले, \q और कबरबेरी भी इच्छा न जगाए, \q क्योंकि हर कोई अपने सदा के घर को जाता है, \q और विलाप करनेवाले गलियों में घूमते हैं,
hi.R: लोग ऊँची जगहों से और गली के ख़तरों से डरेंगे। \q बादाम का पेड़ फूलेगा, और टिड्डा घिसटता हुआ चलेगा, \q और मन की इच्छा मिट जाएगी। \q यह सब इसलिए होता है कि लोग अपने सदा के घर की ओर जा रहे हैं, \q और विलाप करनेवाले गलियों में घूम रहे हैं।

ru.L: и высоты страшатся они, и страхи на дороге, \q и расцветает миндальное дерево, и волочится кузнечик, \q и иссякает каперс; \q ведь идёт человек в дом своей вечности, \q и кружат по улице оплакивающие,
ru.B: когда люди боятся высоты и опасностей на дороге, \q когда цветёт миндальное дерево и кузнечик еле волочит ноги, \q и каперс больше не пробуждает желания, \q потому что каждый уходит в свой вечный дом \q и плакальщики ходят по улицам,
ru.R: Люди будут бояться высоты и опасностей на улице. \q Миндальное дерево зацветёт, кузнечик будет еле волочиться, \q и желание исчезнет. \q Всё это происходит потому, что люди уходят в свой вечный дом, \q а на улицах ходят плакальщики.

uk.L: також висоти бояться, і страхіття [є] на дорозі, \q і зацвітає мигдаль, і тягнеться коник, \q і зникає каперс; \q бо йде людина до свого вічного дому, \q і ходять по вулиці плакальники,
uk.B: коли люди бояться висоти й небезпек на дорозі, \q коли зацвітає мигдаль і ледве тягнеться коник, \q і каперс уже не будить бажання, \q бо кожен іде до свого вічного дому, \q і плакальники ходять по вулицях,
uk.R: Люди боятимуться високих місць і небезпек на вулиці. \q Зацвіте мигдаль, і ледве тягтиметься коник, \q і бажання зникне. \q Усе це стається тому, що люди йдуть до свого вічного дому, \q а плакальники ходять по вулицях.

decisions.choice: the almond tree blossoms: perhaps the white hair of age
alternatives: spring returns while the old person fades
decisions.reason: The almond tree blooms in late winter with white blossoms. Many read it as white hair. Others take it as a sign of new life in nature, set against a human life that is ending.

decisions.choice: the grasshopper drags itself along: a creature made to leap that can only crawl
alternatives: the grasshopper is a burden (even something light weighs heavy)
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to drag oneself along or to be a burden. The grasshopper, which normally springs, moves slowly and stiffly, like the old. Or even a grasshopper becomes too heavy to carry.

decisions.choice: the caper-berry fails: appetite and desire fade
decisions.reason: The word (*'aviyonah*) appears only here. It is usually taken as the caper-berry, which was eaten to stir appetite and desire; the ancient Greek translation has "the caper". The word also looks like the word for "desire". Either way, the appetite for life is gone.

decisions.choice: his eternal house: the grave
decisions.reason: The grave is a person's lasting home (Psalm 49:12). The house of the poem gives way to the house no one leaves.

decisions.choice: the mourners go around in the street: the funeral is being prepared
decisions.reason: Mourners, some of them hired, walked through the streets wailing at a death (Jeremiah 9:16-17; Amos 5:16).

decisions.choice: they are afraid of a height: the old fear high places and the dangers of the road
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it is the people of the house, the old. A climb or a walk outside becomes frightening.

decisions.choice: desire will be gone

decisions.choice: the silver cord and the golden bowl: a precious lamp falls and its light goes out
alternatives: parts of the body, such as the spine and the skull
a single picture of a golden lamp hanging by a silver chain
decisions.reason: The silver cord and the golden bowl are most often read as a lamp, its oil bowl hanging by a silver chain (compare the bowl of the lampstand in Zechariah 4:2-3). When the cord breaks, the bowl falls, and the light goes out: life ends. The costly metals show how precious life is. Some read the cord and bowl as parts of the body, as with the house of verse 3.

decisions.choice: the jar at the spring and the wheel at the cistern: water can no longer be drawn
decisions.reason: The jar for carrying water is broken at the spring, and the wheel or pulley for lowering a bucket is broken at the cistern. Water, the source of life, can no longer be drawn. Readers who see the body here take them as organs such as the heart.

decisions.choice: is snapped, as the scribes read it

decisions.choice: dust to the earth, spirit to God: creation undone
decisions.reason: God formed the first human from dust and breathed into him the breath of life (Genesis 2:7), and said, "to dust you shall return" (Genesis 3:19). At death the two part: the body returns to the earth, and the life God gave returns to him (Psalm 104:29; Job 34:14-15).

decisions.choice: the spirit: the breath of life that God gives
decisions.reason: The word (*ruach*) is breath, wind or spirit. Here it is the life God breathes into a person. Earlier Qoheleth asked who knows whether the human spirit goes upward (3:21); here he says it returns to God who gave it. The verse says where life comes from and goes; it does not describe what lies beyond. Readers differ on how much more it implies.

decisions.choice: and: the last line of the poem
decisions.reason: This verse ends the long sentence begun in verse 1, and Qoheleth's own words, which began in 1:12.

records.literal_gloss: Breath of breaths, says the Qoheleth; the all [is] breath.

en.L: Breath of breaths, says Qoheleth; everything [is] breath.
en.B: Breath upon breath, says the Teacher. Everything is a breath.
en.R: Nothing lasts! says the Teacher. Everything passes like a breath.

es.L: Soplo de soplos, dice Qohélet; todo [es] soplo.
es.B: Soplo tras soplo, dice el Maestro. Todo es un soplo.
es.R: ¡Nada dura!, dice el Maestro. Todo pasa como un soplo.

fr.L: Souffle des souffles, dit Qohéleth ; tout [est] souffle.
fr.B: Souffle sur souffle, dit le Maître. Tout n’est qu’un souffle.
fr.R: Rien ne dure ! dit le Maître. Tout passe comme un souffle.

sw.L: Pumzi ya pumzi, asema Kohelethi; kila kitu [ni] pumzi.
sw.B: Pumzi juu ya pumzi, asema Mwalimu. Kila kitu ni pumzi tu.
sw.R: Hakuna kinachodumu! asema Mwalimu. Kila kitu kinapita kama pumzi.

vi.L: Hơi thở của hơi thở, Cô-hê-lết nói; mọi sự [là] hơi thở.
vi.B: Hơi thở nối hơi thở, Người Thầy nói. Mọi sự chỉ là một hơi thở.
vi.R: Chẳng có gì tồn tại! Người Thầy nói. Mọi sự đều qua đi như một hơi thở.

ko.L: 입김 중의 입김, 코헬렛이 말한다. 모든 것이 입김이다.
ko.B: 입김 또 입김, 스승이 말한다. 모든 것이 한낱 입김이다.
ko.R: 아무것도 남지 않는다! 스승이 말한다. 모든 것이 입김처럼 지나간다.

pt.L: Sopro de sopros, diz Qohélet; tudo [é] sopro.
pt.B: Sopro sobre sopro, diz o Mestre. Tudo é um sopro.
pt.R: Nada dura! diz o Mestre. Tudo passa como um sopro.

am.L: የእስትንፋስ እስትንፋስ፣ ይላል ቆሔሌት፤ ሁሉም እስትንፋስ [ነው]።
am.B: እስትንፋስ፣ ፍጹም እስትንፋስ፣ ይላል መምህሩ። ሁሉም እስትንፋስ ነው።
am.R: ምንም አይዘልቅም! ይላል መምህሩ። ሁሉም ነገር እንደ እስትንፋስ ያልፋል።

hi.L: साँसों की साँस, कोहेलेत कहता है; सब कुछ साँस [है]।
hi.B: साँस पर साँस, उपदेशक कहता है। सब कुछ एक साँस है।
hi.R: कुछ भी नहीं टिकता! उपदेशक कहता है। सब कुछ साँस की तरह बीत जाता है।

ru.L: Дуновение дуновений, — говорит Когелет, — всё — дуновение.
ru.B: Дуновение за дуновением, — говорит Учитель. — Всё — лишь дуновение.
ru.R: Всё мимолётно! — говорит Учитель. — Всё проходит, как лёгкое дыхание.

uk.L: Подих подихів, каже Когелет; усе — подих.
uk.B: Подих над подихами, каже Учитель. Усе — лише подих.
uk.R: Ніщо не триває! — каже Учитель. — Усе минає, як подих.

decisions.choice: breath of breaths: the cry that opened the book, repeated at its close
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1:2 in a shorter form. Qoheleth's words begin and end with the same cry, and everything between is framed by it. See the main note on *hevel* at 1:2.

decisions.choice: breath of breaths: the most fleeting breath, utter breath
decisions.reason: Putting a word with its own plural is a Hebrew way of saying "the most" or "the greatest" ("the Song of Songs", "the holy of holies"). See 1:2.

decisions.choice: says Qoheleth: the frame of the book speaks again
decisions.reason: Here the voice that introduced Qoheleth in 1:1-2 speaks of him again in the third person, and goes on doing so to the end of the book (verses 9-14). The name here has the article, "the Qoheleth", as if it were a title (compare 7:27).

decisions.choice: Breath of breaths ... everything is breath (L); Breath upon breath ... Everything is a breath (B); Nothing lasts! Everything passes like a breath (R)
decisions.reason: The founder's settled wording for the cry of 1:2 and 12:8, in the same words as 1:2 at each level. The shorter verse leaves out the repeated "breath of breaths" ("Nothing lasts!" at Readable).

decisions.choice: Qoheleth (L); the Teacher (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for *qohelet* (see 1:1). Literal keeps it as a name, without the article. No quotation marks are used, as at 1:2.

decisions.choice: the settled wording of 1:2 in its shorter form
decisions.reason: The cry repeats 1:2, so it takes the Spanish settled for 1:2 at each level ("soplo", "Qohélet" / "el Maestro"), leaving out the repeated half as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the settled wording of 1:2 in its shorter form
decisions.reason: The cry repeats 1:2, so it takes the French settled for 1:2 at each level (« souffle », « Qohéleth » / « le Maître »), leaving out the repeated half as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the settled wording of 1:2 in its shorter form
decisions.reason: The cry repeats 1:2, so it takes the Swahili settled for 1:2 at each level ("pumzi", "Kohelethi" / "Mwalimu"), leaving out the repeated half as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the settled wording of 1:2 in its shorter form
decisions.reason: The cry repeats 1:2, so it takes the Vietnamese settled for 1:2 at each level ("hơi thở", "Cô-hê-lết" / "Người Thầy"), leaving out the repeated half as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the settled wording of 1:2 in its shorter form
decisions.reason: The cry repeats 1:2, so it takes the Korean settled for 1:2 at each level ("입김", "코헬렛" / "스승"), leaving out the repeated half as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the wording of 1:2, level by level
decisions.reason: The book closes with the cry it opened with, a little shorter: each level keeps the Amharic of 1:2 ("የእስትንፋስ እስትንፋስ፣ ይላል ቆሔሌት" L; "እስትንፋስ፣ ፍጹም እስትንፋስ፣ ይላል መምህሩ" B; "ምንም አይዘልቅም! ይላል መምህሩ" R). The Hebrew has the article on Qoheleth here; Literal still writes the name, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: the motto in the words of 1:2 at each level
decisions.reason: The cry that opened the book closes it (m1), in the same Hindi words as 1:2 at each level; the shorter verse leaves out the repeated half, as the Hebrew and the English do.

decisions.choice: "कोहेलेत" (L); "उपदेशक" (B, R); no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The book's wording for Qoheleth (see 1:1). The frame of the book speaks again (m3); as at 1:2, no quotation marks are used.

decisions.choice: Дуновение дуновений (L); Дуновение за дуновением (B); Всё мимолётно! (R)
decisions.reason: The cry that opened the book (1:2), in the same words at each level, shorter here as in the Hebrew (m1). Never the Synodal's суета сует (see 1:2).

decisions.choice: Когелет (L); Учитель (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for qohelet (see 1:1); the frame speaks again (m3) and takes dashes, not quotation marks.

source.text: וְיֹתֵ֕ר שֶׁהָיָ֥ה קֹהֶ֖לֶת חָכָ֑ם ע֗וֹד לִמַּד־דַּ֨עַת֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאִזֵּ֣ן וְחִקֵּ֔ר תִּקֵּ֖ן מְשָׁלִ֥ים הַרְבֵּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And further, that was Qoheleth wise, still he taught knowledge the people, and he weighed and searched out [and] set in order proverbs many.

en.L: And further, besides Qoheleth being wise, he also taught the people knowledge; and he weighed and searched out [and] set in order many proverbs.
en.B: Besides being wise, the Teacher also taught the people knowledge. He weighed and studied and arranged many proverbs.
en.R: The Teacher was wise, and he also taught the people what he knew. He listened to many wise sayings, studied them, and put them in order.

es.L: Y además, aparte de que Qohélet era sabio, también enseñó conocimiento al pueblo; y sopesó e investigó [y] ordenó muchos proverbios.
es.B: Además de ser sabio, el Maestro también enseñó conocimiento al pueblo. Sopesó, estudió y ordenó muchos proverbios.
es.R: El Maestro era sabio, y además le enseñaba a la gente lo que sabía. Escuchó muchos dichos sabios, los estudió y los puso en orden.

fr.L: Et de plus, outre que Qohéleth était sage, il a encore enseigné la connaissance au peuple ; et il a pesé et examiné, [et] mis en ordre de nombreux proverbes.
fr.B: Non seulement le Maître était sage, mais il a aussi enseigné la connaissance au peuple. Il a pesé, étudié et mis en ordre de nombreux proverbes.
fr.R: Le Maître était sage, et il a aussi enseigné aux gens ce qu’il savait. Il a écouté beaucoup de paroles de sagesse, il les a étudiées et les a mises en ordre.

sw.L: Na zaidi, licha ya Kohelethi kuwa na hekima, aliwafundisha watu maarifa pia; naye alipima na kuchunguza [na] kupanga mithali nyingi.
sw.B: Mbali na kuwa na hekima, Mwalimu aliwafundisha watu maarifa pia. Alipima, akachunguza na kupanga mithali nyingi.
sw.R: Mwalimu alikuwa na hekima, na pia aliwafundisha watu yale aliyoyajua. Alisikiliza misemo mingi ya hekima, akaichunguza na kuipanga.

vi.L: Và hơn nữa, ngoài việc Cô-hê-lết là người khôn ngoan, ông còn dạy tri thức cho dân chúng; và ông đã cân nhắc, tra cứu [và] sắp xếp nhiều châm ngôn.
vi.B: Ngoài việc là người khôn ngoan, Người Thầy còn dạy tri thức cho dân chúng. Ông đã cân nhắc, nghiên cứu và sắp xếp nhiều châm ngôn.
vi.R: Người Thầy là người khôn ngoan, và ông còn dạy cho dân chúng những điều ông biết. Ông đã lắng nghe nhiều lời khôn ngoan, nghiên cứu và sắp xếp chúng cho có thứ tự.

ko.L: 더 나아가, 코헬렛은 지혜로웠을 뿐 아니라 백성에게 지식을 가르쳤고, 또 많은 잠언을 저울질하고 연구하여 [그것들을] 정리했다.
ko.B: 스승은 지혜로웠을 뿐 아니라 백성에게 지식을 가르쳤다. 그는 많은 잠언을 저울질하고 연구하고 정리했다.
ko.R: 스승은 지혜로운 사람이었고, 자기가 아는 것을 백성에게 가르쳤다. 그는 지혜로운 말을 많이 듣고 연구해서 차례대로 정리했다.

pt.L: E além disso, além de Qohélet ser sábio, ele também ensinou conhecimento ao povo; e ponderou e investigou [e] pôs em ordem muitos provérbios.
pt.B: Além de ser sábio, o Mestre também ensinou conhecimento ao povo. Ele pesou, estudou e organizou muitos provérbios.
pt.R: O Mestre era sábio, e também ensinou ao povo o que sabia. Ele ouviu muitos ditados sábios, estudou esses ditados e os pôs em ordem.

am.L: ደግሞም ቆሔሌት ጠቢብ ከመሆኑ በላይ ለሕዝቡ እውቀትን አስተማረ፤ መዘነ፣ መረመረም፤ ብዙ ምሳሌዎችንም በሥርዓት አደራጀ።
